title: Sterile technique at the bench
summary: The non-negotiable habits that keep your cultures and reagents from contamination. Practice this before every other wet-bench protocol.

reagents.name: Bunsen burner or electric loop sterilizer (BSL-1 only)

hazardsMd: Open flames and BSCs don't mix — Bunsen burners disrupt BSC airflow and are fire risks. Use only on the open bench at BSL-1; switch to electric sterilizers in the BSC.
contentUndergrad:
## Why sterile technique matters

A single contaminated reagent can ruin a week of work — and worse, it can quietly skew results for months before you catch it. Sterile technique is the discipline of treating the environment as a hostile place full of microbes you don't want.

Key principles:
- **Spray, then move.** 70% ethanol on every gloved surface before it crosses into your work area.
- **Open into the airflow.** In a BSC, never block the front grille. On the open bench, work close to the flame's updraft.
- **One thing at a time.** Cap a tube before reaching for the next reagent.

steps.title: Set up your work area
steps.instructionMd:
1. Wipe the bench or BSC interior with 70% ethanol, top-to-bottom and back-to-front.
2. Spray every item you'll bring into the work area before placing it.
3. Lay out tools: clean side on the left, waste container on the right.
steps.safetyNotesMd: If using a Bunsen burner on the open bench, confirm the gas valve is undamaged before lighting.
steps.verificationMd: Bench/BSC surface looks visibly damp from ethanol but already drying. All needed items are inside the work area; nothing needs to be reached for mid-procedure.

steps.title: Prepare your gloves
steps.instructionMd: Spray gloved hands with 70% ethanol. Rub thoroughly. Re-spray any time you touch something outside the work area.
steps.verificationMd: Gloves shine briefly with ethanol then dry. No visible debris on fingertips.

steps.title: Open containers with one hand
steps.instructionMd: Hold the tube/bottle in your dominant hand. Use your pinky-and-ring fingers to grip the cap; never set a cap face-down on the bench. Pour or aspirate, then immediately recap.
steps.verificationMd: Cap stays in your hand the whole time. The mouth of the tube/bottle never touches the bench surface.

steps.title: Aspirate carefully
steps.instructionMd: Tip the pipette into the liquid only as far as you need. Don't blow bubbles; bubble splatter spreads contamination. Eject tips into a sealed waste container, not on the bench.
steps.verificationMd: No droplets on the outside of the pipette barrel. No tips loose on the bench.

steps.title: Decontaminate when done
steps.instructionMd: Wipe the entire work surface with 70% ethanol. Bag biological waste per the biohazard-waste protocol. Wash hands after removing gloves.
steps.verificationMd: Bench/BSC is dry, free of debris, and the spray bottle is back in its place. Sharps and biohazard bags are sealed.
